stem: A manufacturer’s AI committee can recommend suspension but has no approved decision rights. A customer-facing agent will enter production next week. What should the sponsor resolve before approval?

options.text: Ask internal audit to operate the release gate.
options.explanation: Audit should independently assure controls rather than own their operation.

options.text: Let the model supplier choose approval thresholds.
options.explanation: The supplier cannot set the customer’s risk authority or business limits.

options.text: Approve the charter’s authority, owners and escalation paths.
options.explanation: A committee needs a mandate and accountable decisions before it can govern release.

options.text: Increase the committee’s meeting frequency.
options.explanation: More meetings do not establish decision authority.

stem: An occupational-safety AI pilot has a technical owner, but no one can approve the consequences of missed hazards. Which gap most directly prevents a defensible use decision?

options.text: An accountable business/safety risk owner with defined authority.
options.explanation: Technical ownership does not establish authority over the consequences.

options.text: An annual policy acknowledgement from users.
options.explanation: Acknowledgement does not assign decision rights.

options.text: A vendor indemnity covering false negatives.
options.explanation: Financial terms do not establish local safety accountability.

options.text: A second model architecture for comparison.
options.explanation: A model comparison may help evaluation but does not close accountability.

stem: A supplier presents ISO/IEC 42001 certification for its AI management system. Procurement asks whether this proves the proposed customer-credit application is lawful and accurate. Which answer is best supported?

options.text: Replace local testing with the supplier’s management review.
options.explanation: A management review does not establish performance for this population.

options.text: Check certificate scope and separately assess the application and legal duties.
options.explanation: A scoped management-system certificate is evidence, not blanket product approval.

options.text: Treat the certificate as the system’s conformity assessment.
options.explanation: Management-system certification and statutory conformity are distinct instruments.

options.text: Approve the use if the certification body is accredited.
options.explanation: Accreditation does not remove use-specific evaluation and duties.

stem: An organization hosts an unchanged third-party model internally. A reviewer labels it the model’s developer solely because it operates the server. What should the reviewer do?

options.text: Ask the cloud provider to accept the organization’s deployer duties.
options.explanation: Its own applicable obligations cannot simply be reassigned by request.

options.text: Determine the actual model/system role from development, supply, intended use and law.
options.explanation: Hosting alone does not establish every statutory or development role.

options.text: Apply provider obligations to every hosted model automatically.
options.explanation: The conclusion needs the actual definitions and facts.

options.text: Exclude legal-role analysis because no data leaves the premises.
options.explanation: Local processing does not remove legal duties.

stem: A factory’s internal assistant processes personal information. A manager requires a FRIA merely because the system uses AI. What is the most appropriate correction?

options.text: Require every employee to consent to avoid assessment.
options.explanation: Consent is not a universal substitute for assessment or lawful processing.

options.text: Assume internal systems are outside all AI obligations.
options.explanation: Internal operation alone does not establish exemption.

options.text: Replace the FRIA with a supplier’s model card in every case.
options.explanation: A model card does not discharge a statutory assessment obligation.

options.text: Check the qualifying deployer, high-risk use and applicable legal trigger.
options.explanation: A FRIA has defined scope; other risk/privacy reviews may still be required.

stem: A multinational proposes employee performance scoring. Legal, security and HR have reviewed it, but affected workers have had no route to raise contextual concerns. What should governance add?

options.text: A larger held-out technical benchmark without process changes.
options.explanation: Benchmarking cannot alone resolve stakeholder participation and redress.

options.text: A disclaimer stating that AI recommendations may be wrong.
options.explanation: Disclosure alone does not provide participation or recourse.

options.text: Proportionate engagement and a documented review/redress mechanism.
options.explanation: Affected stakeholders can identify harms and need a usable contest route.

options.text: Supplier approval of the organization’s workforce policy.
options.explanation: The supplier does not replace local employment and governance decisions.

stem: A policy says “use AI responsibly” but does not define allowed data or approval requirements. Which change most directly makes the policy usable?

options.text: Add a longer preamble describing AI innovation.
options.explanation: Background does not specify required behaviour.

options.text: State scope, permitted/prohibited uses, data rules, owners and escalation.
options.explanation: These decisions turn general intent into actionable expectations.

options.text: Purchase a gateway before defining enforcement rules.
options.explanation: A tool needs an authorized policy to implement.

options.text: Require staff to sign the existing wording twice yearly.
options.explanation: Acknowledging ambiguity does not remove it.

stem: A board permits AI maintenance recommendations but no autonomous safety-critical changes. Which requirement is an operational control threshold?

options.text: Reject safety-setting tool calls without a valid supervisor approval.
options.explanation: The rule creates an enforceable boundary tied to the appetite decision.

options.text: The AI strategy supports efficient maintenance.
options.explanation: This is an objective, not an enforceable threshold.

options.text: The organization has a cautious approach to safety risk.
options.explanation: This is broad appetite language rather than a specific operating check.

options.text: The supplier is committed to responsible automation.
options.explanation: A supplier assertion does not implement the local limit.

stem: An approved pilot requests a 30-day exception to a nonmandatory documentation standard. Which record best supports the decision?

options.text: Scope, reason, residual risk, approver, compensating controls and expiry.
options.explanation: A time-bound exception needs ownership and a reviewable risk decision.

options.text: A waiver of all related regulatory duties for the pilot.
options.explanation: An internal exception cannot waive mandatory obligations.

options.text: A permanent exemption signed by the project developer.
options.explanation: This exceeds the request and may lack authority.

options.text: A verbal agreement to finish documentation after production.
options.explanation: It lacks scope, evidence, expiry and accountable approval.

stem: Monitoring confirms staff are exporting confidential plans to an unsanctioned assistant. The response plan authorizes restriction of such export. What is the best combined action?

options.text: Wait for a usability survey before restricting any export.
options.explanation: Known exposure already justifies the authorized response.

options.text: Restrict the known exposure while investigating unmet workflow needs.
options.explanation: Containment and cause-based improvement can proceed together.

options.text: Apply sanctions without examining how the work is performed.
options.explanation: Enforcement alone may leave the cause and discovery gaps unresolved.

options.text: Publish the same policy again without changing controls.
options.explanation: Repetition does not contain the observed disclosure.

stem: An AI strategy and risk appetite are already approved. Teams need a repeatable review process. What is the most appropriate next deliverable?

options.text: Another executive appetite statement before any workflow work.
options.explanation: The scenario says the prerequisite decision already exists.

options.text: A list of preferred model brands without use requirements.
options.explanation: Brand choices do not define a repeatable review process.

options.text: A new committee with no relationship to existing governance.
options.explanation: Duplicating governance does not establish the missing procedure.

options.text: A procedure defining intake evidence, checks, decisions and records.
options.explanation: The missing operational layer translates approved intent into practice.

stem: A proposed LLM invoice approver has higher review costs and more false approvals than the current rules engine. Which recommendation is most defensible?

options.text: Proceed because adopting AI is an explicit strategic goal.
options.explanation: A broad strategy does not establish value or acceptable error here.

options.text: Increase the model’s autonomy to offset review costs.
options.explanation: Removing review can increase harmful approvals.

options.text: Retain the rules baseline and investigate narrower AI uses with measurable benefit.
options.explanation: The evidence supports the simpler approval method while allowing justified alternatives.

options.text: Exclude error consequences from the cost-benefit comparison.
options.explanation: Failure costs are material to the use decision.

stem: A new support assistant is in the asset register as “AI chatbot.” Responders cannot identify its model version or data dependencies. What is the most useful improvement?

options.text: Link the use to versioned models, corpora, tools, owners and approval evidence.
options.explanation: Dependency and version information enables scoping and accountable decisions.

options.text: Rename it “enterprise AI chatbot” for consistency.
options.explanation: A name change does not add the missing evidence.

options.text: Record only the hostname because all data is external.
options.explanation: Endpoints alone omit relevant model and data dependencies.

options.text: Leave details with the vendor until an incident occurs.
options.explanation: Delayed discovery undermines response and governance.

stem: A SaaS vendor enables an AI summarizer between annual inventory reviews. Which process best reduces the resulting visibility gap?

options.text: An inventory limited to systems that procurement bought as AI.
options.explanation: AI can enter existing services or development dependencies.

options.text: A more detailed annual questionnaire without interim monitoring.
options.explanation: Annual-only collection can still miss months of changed exposure.

options.text: Event-driven change discovery with periodic independent reconciliation.
options.explanation: Capability changes require timely updates as well as completeness checks.

options.text: A policy forbidding vendors from changing software without verification.
options.explanation: A policy needs monitoring and contractual/technical enforcement.

stem: A dataset is classified internal but contains material licensed for retrieval only. A team proposes fine-tuning on it. Which determination is needed?

options.text: Approve because the dataset is not marked confidential.
options.explanation: A sensitivity label is not a licence or lawful-use decision.

options.text: Obtain a faster training environment before reviewing rights.
options.explanation: Infrastructure capacity does not establish permission to train.

options.text: Remove the classification label after tokenization.
options.explanation: Tokenization does not remove rights or sensitivity.

options.text: Assess permitted use and rights separately from sensitivity.
options.explanation: Internal classification does not authorize every processing purpose.

stem: A retired assistant’s source documents are deleted, but its vector store and cached answers remain available. Which finding is most direct?

options.text: No further action is needed if the original owner left the company.
options.explanation: Ownership transfer and retention duties remain.

options.text: The model necessarily learned the documents during every query.
options.explanation: RAG inference does not necessarily update weights.

options.text: Retirement did not trace and handle the derived data estate.
options.explanation: Deletion must reach relevant derivatives under the approved retention rules.

options.text: The vector entries are anonymous because they are numeric.
options.explanation: Vectors and stored chunks can reveal sensitive content.

stem: Employees fear reporting unapproved AI use because the discovery email promises automatic discipline. What improves the inventory’s reliability?

options.text: Remove user surveys because technical discovery is complete by definition.
options.explanation: Technical tooling may miss personal accounts, embedded use or offline models.

options.text: Publish a clear, proportionate disclosure process and any scoped amnesty.
options.explanation: Reducing avoidable reporting barriers improves discovery without promising unlimited immunity.

options.text: Promise that deliberate misconduct can never have consequences.
options.explanation: Unconditional immunity may be inappropriate and not credible.

options.text: Rely solely on staff who voluntarily admitted use already.
options.explanation: This leaves the same discovery bias in place.

stem: A board dashboard reports 98% of known AI uses have current approvals. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: Coverage is high within the discovered estate; effectiveness needs additional evidence.
options.explanation: The denominator and metric describe coverage, not all unknown uses or control outcomes.

options.text: The organization has reduced harmful AI outcomes by 98%.
options.explanation: The metric does not measure harm reduction.

options.text: Every approved system’s controls operate effectively.
options.explanation: Approval status alone does not test operation.

options.text: Undiscovered AI use is immaterial because approvals are current.
options.explanation: Unknown uses are absent from the denominator.

stem: A gateway’s policy is approved. Which measure most directly tests whether it prevents unauthorized model traffic?

options.text: Success/failure on representative prohibited flows, including bypass paths.
options.explanation: This directly evaluates the claimed enforcement behaviour.

options.text: Percentage of staff who recognize the gateway’s name.
options.explanation: Name recognition does not establish prevention effectiveness.

options.text: Number of policy pages published this quarter.
options.explanation: Publication measures activity, not enforcement.

options.text: Count of gateway vendor demonstrations attended.
options.explanation: Demonstrations do not test the actual deployment.

stem: Eight low-tier assistants share one inference provider. Separate assessments do not consider simultaneous outage. What should enterprise risk review add?

options.text: Combined dependency impact and correlated-failure treatment.
options.explanation: Individually tolerable uses can create material aggregated exposure.

options.text: Eight independent supplier certifications for the same service.
options.explanation: Duplicated evidence does not resolve concentration.

options.text: A separate risk colour for each assistant without dependency analysis.
options.explanation: Different colours do not reveal the common cause.

options.text: Remove the assistants from local registers once aggregated.
options.explanation: Local ownership and controls are still needed.

stem: An AI security roadmap lists useful controls but no funding, owners or milestones. What is the primary program-management weakness?

options.text: The roadmap uses existing security processes.
options.explanation: Integration is generally useful, not the weakness described.

options.text: Implementation is not assigned, resourced or reviewable.
options.explanation: A roadmap needs accountable delivery and progress evidence.

options.text: Every control must be replaced by one consolidated product.
options.explanation: Consolidation does not substitute for planning.

options.text: The roadmap lacks a separate AI-only identity platform.
options.explanation: A parallel stack is not inherently necessary.

stem: The security team operates a production AI filter and also signs its only assurance report. Which change best improves independent challenge?

options.text: Declare security always second line, regardless of its activities.
options.explanation: Labels do not remove the conflict in responsibilities.

options.text: Arrange risk-proportionate assurance separate from the filter’s operators.
options.explanation: Independence concerns the operated control, not simply department names.

options.text: Assign internal audit daily filter tuning.
options.explanation: Operating the control would compromise audit assurance.

options.text: Eliminate operational logs to avoid review bias.
options.explanation: Removing evidence weakens rather than strengthens assurance.

stem: An agent is actively sending customer records to an unapproved destination. The incident plan authorizes the commander to revoke its credentials. What should happen first operationally?

options.text: Revoke or restrict the export path while preserving evidence and coordinating response.
options.explanation: Known active disclosure warrants authorized containment alongside investigation.

options.text: Retrain the model before restricting its credentials.
options.explanation: Retraining delays an available containment action.

options.text: Ask all customers to consent to the current exports.
options.explanation: Consent does not retrospectively authorize an incident.

options.text: Wait for the next AI committee meeting to assign a risk tier.
options.explanation: Routine governance timing does not fit ongoing harm.

stem: Containment of a breach is incomplete, but a legally applicable initial-notification deadline is approaching. Which response is appropriate?

options.text: Have the model decide whether notification is legally necessary.
options.explanation: Legal applicability requires accountable review rather than unverified model judgment.

options.text: Wait until all uncertainty is eliminated before notifying.
options.explanation: Investigation uncertainty does not suspend an applicable deadline.

options.text: Replace required notification with an internal incident log.
options.explanation: Internal documentation does not discharge external duties.

options.text: Submit the required initial report and update it as facts develop.
options.explanation: Reporting obligations can run in parallel with containment and investigation.

stem: Responders need traces containing personal data while a normal deletion schedule is due. What is the best evidence-preservation action?

options.text: Delete all traces immediately because schedules can never change.
options.explanation: A lawful justified hold may require preservation.

options.text: Suspend every retention rule indefinitely across the organization.
options.explanation: A blanket indefinite hold is not justified by the described need.

options.text: Apply an authorized, scoped hold with basis, access limits and review date.
options.explanation: Preserve relevant evidence proportionately and document why.

options.text: Copy the traces to personal storage for investigator convenience.
options.explanation: This introduces unnecessary access and retention risk.

stem: A maintenance model remains available but its missed-failure rate crosses an approved safety trigger. Which continuity response is most appropriate?

options.text: Invoke the tested safe fallback under the defined authority.
options.explanation: Continuity must address trustworthy operation, not availability alone.

options.text: Keep using it until the service becomes unavailable.
options.explanation: The safety trigger already indicates unacceptable operation.

options.text: Remove the monitoring threshold during retraining.
options.explanation: Suppressing the trigger hides the risk.

options.text: Increase server capacity to restore confidence.
options.explanation: Capacity does not address the measured decision failure.

stem: A procurement process can tolerate two hours of interruption, but its fallback queue clears only half the daily workload. What must the exercise resolve?

options.text: Whether the fallback has the same brand as the primary model.
options.explanation: Brand identity does not determine continuity capability.

options.text: Whether the business can omit recovery objectives for AI.
options.explanation: AI dependence still needs impact-based objectives.

options.text: Fallback capacity, prioritization and recovery objectives under realistic load.
options.explanation: A documented fallback is insufficient if it cannot sustain required service.

options.text: Whether a longer model context window is available.
options.explanation: Context size does not establish fallback capacity.

stem: A poisoned model has been replaced. Which evidence best supports return to service?

options.text: A supplier promise that retraining usually works.
options.explanation: A general assurance does not verify this release.

options.text: Clean provenance, attack-path/regression tests, staged recovery and authorized sign-off.
options.explanation: Recovery needs evidence that the cause and affected controls were addressed.

options.text: A quiet monitoring dashboard for ten minutes without validation.
options.explanation: Absence of visible symptoms is insufficient.

options.text: A stronger system prompt with the same compromised artifact.
options.explanation: Instructions do not establish that poisoning was removed.

stem: A risk register entry says only “AI hallucination: high.” Which revision best supports a treatment decision?

options.text: Replace “high” with a red icon.
options.explanation: Presentation does not improve the underlying analysis.

options.text: Assign the entry to “everyone using AI.”
options.explanation: Collective concern does not establish accountable ownership.

options.text: Describe the use, affected parties, failure event, consequences, assumptions and owner.
options.explanation: A scoped scenario connects uncertainty to a decision and accountable treatment.

options.text: Add every attack name to the same entry.
options.explanation: Unscoped lists obscure distinct mechanisms and consequences.

stem: A supplier assistant’s risk was assessed before entitlement controls. It is assessed again after verified enforcement. What does the second assessment primarily describe?

options.text: The organization’s overall risk appetite.
options.explanation: Appetite is a governance decision rather than this assessment result.

options.text: A guarantee that the risk is eliminated.
options.explanation: Controls reduce or constrain exposure without establishing zero risk.

options.text: Residual risk under the evidenced controls and stated assumptions.
options.explanation: Residual exposure considers implemented controls rather than assumed perfect protection.

options.text: Inherent risk with no reference to controls.
options.explanation: That describes the defined pre-control view.

stem: A scenario assumes a mean 0.2 loss events annually and $500,000 mean loss per event, with that severity applicable to the events. What is the rough annual expected loss?

options.text: $100,000, while retaining uncertainty and severe-tail analysis.
options.explanation: Multiplying the stated means gives this simplified expectation; it is not a worst case.

options.text: $500,000, because frequency does not affect annual exposure.
options.explanation: Frequency is part of the annual expectation.

options.text: $0, because fewer than one event per year means no events.
options.explanation: A fractional annual mean represents events over time, not impossibility.

options.text: $2,500,000, by dividing loss by frequency.
options.explanation: Division does not calculate the stated expected annual loss.

stem: Two treatments have the same mean annual loss reduction. One leaves a rare catastrophic safety failure above tolerance. What should the risk owner consider?

options.text: Ignore severe outcomes because they are infrequent.
options.explanation: Low probability does not remove material impact or obligations.

options.text: Only choose the lower purchase price.
options.explanation: Price alone ignores the intolerable outcome.

options.text: Distribution tails, safety limits and legal constraints in addition to the mean.
options.explanation: Expected value alone does not establish acceptable risk.

options.text: Accept the risk if the supplier offers a model card.
options.explanation: Documentation does not authorize exposure beyond limits.

stem: A business executive requests acceptance of a legally prohibited AI use because anticipated savings exceed expected fines. Which advice is appropriate?

options.text: Transfer the legal obligation through an indemnity.
options.explanation: An indemnity does not remove the organization’s duty.

options.text: Record a lower risk score to align with the savings.
options.explanation: Changing the score does not change the exposure or legal limit.

options.text: Approve if the executive owns the operating budget.
options.explanation: Budget authority is not authority to permit unlawful activity.

options.text: Reject that acceptance route and seek a lawful redesign or alternative.
options.explanation: Risk acceptance cannot waive a prohibition.

stem: An internal risk assessment measures only company revenue loss from hiring errors. What should an AI impact review add?

options.text: A statement that privacy belongs exclusively to the supplier.
options.explanation: Local data use and effects remain relevant.

options.text: Only the model’s GPU utilization.
options.explanation: Infrastructure utilization does not address the missing harms.

options.text: A prohibition on interviewing affected stakeholders.
options.explanation: Excluding stakeholders can conceal the missing context.

options.text: Effects on applicants, affected groups, oversight and meaningful recourse.
options.explanation: Stakeholder consequences need explicit assessment alongside enterprise loss.

stem: A provider supplies a conformity assessment for a qualifying high-risk application. The qualifying deployer assumes its own FRIA is therefore unnecessary. What is the best correction?

options.text: Treat a procurement approval as a statutory exemption.
options.explanation: An internal decision does not establish exemption.

options.text: Determine and perform the deployer’s applicable assessment using relevant shared evidence.
options.explanation: Product conformity and deployment impacts are distinct responsibilities.

options.text: Require the provider to accept all complaints instead of assessing use.
options.explanation: Complaint routing cannot replace applicable assessment duties.

options.text: Repeat the provider’s assessment under the deployer’s logo only.
options.explanation: Rebranding evidence does not assess local use and impacts.

stem: A model’s approved use expands from maintenance engineers to external customers in a new jurisdiction. Which response is most appropriate?

options.text: Keep approval unchanged because the weights are identical.
options.explanation: System context can change risk without changing weights.

options.text: Reassess purpose, data, impacts, obligations and approval conditions before expansion.
options.explanation: Users and jurisdiction are material changes to the assessed use.

options.text: Wait for an incident to establish whether reassessment was necessary.
options.explanation: The known material change already supplies a review trigger.

options.text: Change only the inventory’s user count.
options.explanation: Recording the change does not evaluate its consequences.

stem: A board asks why a quantified AI-risk estimate is a range rather than one precise dollar value. Which explanation is most accurate?

options.text: A wide range proves the worst case will occur.
options.explanation: Uncertainty is not certainty of the extreme.

options.text: Frequency and severity estimates are uncertain; the range exposes assumptions for decisions.
options.explanation: Expressing uncertainty avoids implying unsupported precision.

options.text: Ranges are used because financial consequences are irrelevant.
options.explanation: The analysis is specifically about consequences for a decision.

options.text: The range removes the need to state the scenario.
options.explanation: Scope and assumptions remain essential.

stem: Residual risk remains within delegated tolerance after verified controls. What makes acceptance defensible over time?

options.text: Disabling metrics so small failures do not reopen the decision.
options.explanation: Removing visibility undermines the conditions of acceptance.

options.text: A developer’s private note that errors are expected.
options.explanation: This lacks acceptance authority and shared evidence.

options.text: A permanent approval with no expiry or triggers.
options.explanation: Risk and context can change.

options.text: A named authorized owner, conditions, review date and monitored reassessment triggers.
options.explanation: Acceptance is an accountable continuing decision.

stem: An attacker repeatedly queries a pricing model to reproduce useful predictions in a competing service. What is the primary objective?

options.text: Membership inference about one customer.
options.explanation: The scenario does not seek training-set inclusion of a record.

options.text: Training-data label flipping.
options.explanation: There is no alteration of training labels.

options.text: A lawful-basis assessment.
options.explanation: This is not the attacker’s described objective.

options.text: Model extraction of useful functionality.
options.explanation: The described target is the model’s capability.

stem: An attacker tests whether a named person appeared in a sensitive medical training set. Which threat is most direct?

options.text: Dependency confusion.
options.explanation: No package-resolution attack is described.

options.text: Concept drift.
options.explanation: A change in input/outcome relationships is not the attack objective.

options.text: Model extraction.
options.explanation: Copying predictive functionality is a different goal.

options.text: Membership inference.
options.explanation: The disclosure sought is inclusion of a particular record or individual.

stem: A classifier is tested with crafted production inputs that cause misclassification. Which build-time technique may reduce that inference-time risk?

options.text: Rate limiting alone, guaranteeing correct classifications.
options.explanation: Rate limits do not guarantee robustness to a crafted individual input.

options.text: Evaluated adversarial training for the relevant threat model.
options.explanation: A training activity can improve resistance to inference-time evasion.

options.text: Deleting deployment logs to hide the decision boundary.
options.explanation: Removing evidence does not repair model robustness.

options.text: Reclassifying the attack as poisoning solely because training is a defence.
options.explanation: Attack stage and defence implementation stage differ.

stem: A model behaves normally except when a rare phrase triggers unauthorized output. The organization acquired it from a public hub. What should investigation consider?

options.text: A backdoor introduced through data, modified weights or a supplied artifact.
options.explanation: A trigger-dependent failure can originate at multiple supply-chain points.

options.text: An instruction to approve the model if the file has a familiar name.
options.explanation: Names do not establish provenance or behaviour.

options.text: A purely availability incident with no need for model analysis.
options.explanation: The described failure changes behaviour and authority.

options.text: A guarantee of harmlessness because average accuracy is high.
options.explanation: Ordinary aggregate evaluation can miss rare triggers.

stem: A recruiter’s assistant reads a resume containing instructions to export other applicants’ data. The sender never uses the assistant’s interface. What is the main application threat?

options.text: Direct administrator configuration.
options.explanation: The sender has not supplied an authorized system instruction.

options.text: A privacy guarantee from RAG.
options.explanation: Retrieval does not make malicious content trustworthy.

options.text: Authorized model retraining from user feedback.
options.explanation: Reading the resume need not update weights or be authorized training.

options.text: Indirect prompt injection through untrusted content.
options.explanation: The instruction enters material read on another user’s behalf.

stem: A model file is safe to parse but the serving library has a remote-code-execution vulnerability. What should vulnerability management do?

options.text: Patch or mitigate the serving stack and retest the affected system.
options.explanation: Ordinary software vulnerabilities remain in scope for AI deployments.

options.text: Rely on the model card instead of verifying deployment exposure.
options.explanation: Documentation does not patch the library.

options.text: Fine-tune the model to refuse exploit requests as the only control.
options.explanation: Instructions do not fix the vulnerable execution environment.

options.text: Exclude the issue because AI has no patch cycle.
options.explanation: The claim confuses model remediation with software patching.

stem: A poisoning incident is contained by disabling high-impact tool actions. The model passes a small normal-use sample afterward. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: The training data is clean because tools are disabled.
options.explanation: Tool permissions do not establish data integrity.

options.text: Containment reduced impact, but underlying remediation still needs validation.
options.explanation: A runtime restriction and ordinary sample do not prove the poisoning removed.

options.text: The normal sample proves all trigger behaviour impossible.
options.explanation: A small nonadversarial sample cannot support that guarantee.

options.text: Every runtime restriction is irrelevant to poisoning response.
options.explanation: Such restrictions can contain consequences even without curing the cause.

stem: An employee receives a convincing video request to change bank details. Which control most directly reduces reliance on the video’s apparent identity?

options.text: Independent verification using an established channel and separate change approval.
options.explanation: Verification and authorization should not depend on the suspect media alone.

options.text: Checking whether the speaker uses the correct accent.
options.explanation: Audio and visual familiarity are vulnerable cues.

options.text: Allowing urgent changes without approval when the face is familiar.
options.explanation: Urgency and recognition do not establish authority.

options.text: Disabling all account-change logs to protect privacy.
options.explanation: Proportionate logging supports fraud detection and investigation.

stem: A red team tests only direct jailbreak prompts against an agent. Which scope addition is most valuable?

options.text: Only the public vendor benchmark score.
options.explanation: A benchmark does not test the local integrations.

options.text: Retrieved content, tools, memory, identities, egress and surrounding infrastructure.
options.explanation: The deployed system has trust boundaries beyond direct user prompts.

options.text: Excluding nontechnical harm because no exploit is required.
options.explanation: Impact and safety failures remain relevant to the risk assessment.

options.text: More direct prompts with no system-boundary analysis.
options.explanation: Volume alone does not close the omitted attack surfaces.

stem: A threat model has a diagram and a list of attacks, but no control owners or verification. Which next step most directly makes it actionable?

options.text: Map prioritized threats to owned controls, test evidence and residual-risk decisions.
options.explanation: A threat model must inform treatment and be validated.

options.text: Add every available attack name without prioritization.
options.explanation: An unprioritized catalogue is not an implementation plan.

options.text: Publish the diagram without reviewing system changes.
options.explanation: Static publication does not maintain relevance or verify controls.

options.text: Treat all risks as transferred because a vendor is involved.
options.explanation: Supplier involvement does not eliminate local responsibilities.

stem: An AI supplier gives a security attestation covering its office IT, but not the hosted inference service. What should procurement do?

options.text: Ask the supplier to rename the office service in the report.
options.explanation: Relabeling does not change what was assessed.

options.text: Obtain relevant scoped evidence and evaluate remaining assurance gaps.
options.explanation: Evidence must address the service and controls being relied on.

options.text: Assume all supplier services share the attested scope.
options.explanation: Scope cannot be inferred from the company name.

options.text: Reject every alternative form of assurance automatically.
options.explanation: Risk-based evidence can include more than one instrument.

stem: A fraud-service supplier can change its model without notice. Customer acceptance thresholds were validated against one version. Which contract provision most directly helps?

options.text: Only a service-availability percentage.
options.explanation: Availability does not establish unchanged decision behaviour.

options.text: A larger indemnity with no operational notification.
options.explanation: Money alone does not permit timely revalidation.

options.text: Defined change notice, impact evidence and workable version/revalidation or exit options.
options.explanation: The customer needs a way to assess and manage changed behaviour.

options.text: A guarantee that the supplier will never update any software.
options.explanation: An absolute freeze is often unworkable and does not address managed change.

stem: A company contracts with an AI SaaS provider, which subcontracts inference hosting. Relative to the company, what is the hosting subcontractor?

options.text: The company’s direct third party solely because it runs inference.
options.explanation: The chain’s relationship, not the technical function, defines this tier.

options.text: A fourth-party dependency in the stated chain.
options.explanation: The SaaS supplier is the direct third party; its subcontractor is the next tier.

options.text: Outside supply-chain review because no direct contract exists.
options.explanation: Indirect dependencies can materially affect risk and continuity.

options.text: An internal first-line employee.
options.explanation: It is an external subcontractor, not company personnel.

stem: A supplier offers broad indemnity for erroneous output. Which risk does this most directly address?

options.text: All regulatory accountability of the customer.
options.explanation: Applicable duties do not disappear through indemnity.

options.text: Guaranteed continuity if the supplier fails.
options.explanation: A payment obligation does not supply operational capacity.

options.text: Some financial exposure, subject to exclusions, limits and collectability.
options.explanation: Indemnity provides a potential financial recovery route, not complete transfer.

options.text: Automatic restoration of customer trust after harm.
options.explanation: Reputation is not restored by a contract clause alone.

stem: A service says customer prompts are not used for training, but retains them for support. What must the customer still assess?

options.text: Whether the prompts are converted to numbers before storage.
options.explanation: Representation does not remove sensitivity.

options.text: Only how many parameters the model has.
options.explanation: Model size does not establish the data-handling conditions.

options.text: Nothing, because no-training means the model sees no data.
options.explanation: Inference and support still process the prompts.

options.text: Retention, access, locations, subprocessors and deletion for the retained data.
options.explanation: No-training terms do not mean no processing or storage.

stem: A critical AI supplier’s exit clause promises deletion but provides no portability, transition period or verification. What should the customer negotiate?

options.text: Usable exports, transition support, dependency handover and deletion evidence.
options.explanation: Exit must support continuity and verify remaining data handling.

options.text: A statement that moving providers always preserves model behaviour.
options.explanation: Equivalent behaviour requires evaluation rather than assumption.

options.text: A lower renewal price instead of an exit plan.
options.explanation: Price does not close continuity and deletion gaps.

options.text: Deletion of all customer evidence before migration starts.
options.explanation: Premature deletion can undermine recovery and assurance.

stem: Two departments independently test the same supplier’s model. Both assume the other verifies tenant isolation and incident notification. What is missing?

options.text: A third identical accuracy test with unchanged assumptions.
options.explanation: More duplicate testing does not assign the omitted duties.

options.text: An explicit responsibility matrix tied to contract and verification evidence.
options.explanation: Unassigned obligations fall between teams despite duplicated tests.

options.text: A separate governance committee for each test team.
options.explanation: Additional committees do not necessarily close ownership.

options.text: A blanket statement that all supplier risks are low.
options.explanation: A label does not resolve responsibilities.

stem: A provider-hosted fine-tune and a self-hosted unchanged model are shortlisted. What comparison is most informative?

options.text: Assume local hosting eliminates all supplier provenance risks.
options.explanation: Upstream data, licences and artifacts remain relevant.

options.text: Assume the hosted fine-tune requires no local use-case validation.
options.explanation: The customer must evaluate its intended use.

options.text: Separate model origin, adaptation, hosting, data flows and change responsibilities.
options.explanation: These independent dimensions determine actual control options and duties.

options.text: Rank fine-tuning and self-hosting as mutually exclusive categories.
options.explanation: A fine-tuned model can also be self-hosted.

stem: An authenticated user asks an assistant about restricted board papers. Retrieval uses a service identity that can read everything. Which change most directly prevents unauthorized context disclosure?

options.text: Encrypt the store while leaving retrieval permissions unchanged.
options.explanation: At-rest encryption does not stop authorized service queries returning forbidden content.

options.text: Enforce the requesting user’s source entitlements before context reaches the model.
options.explanation: Authentication at the interface does not limit a broadly privileged retriever.

options.text: Remove the user’s name from the audit log.
options.explanation: Removing attribution does not restrict retrieval.

options.text: Ask the system prompt not to mention board papers.
options.explanation: Instructions are not an enforceable document-access boundary.

stem: A document contains an instruction to send a summary to an attacker’s URL. The model needs to read the document for a legitimate task. Which defence best bounds the action?

options.text: Allow only authorized destinations and validate export actions outside the model.
options.explanation: Independent egress and action checks limit consequences of malicious instructions.

options.text: Delete all prompts before the model reads any document.
options.explanation: This removes legitimate operation without addressing the required boundary.

options.text: Treat retrieved instructions as administrator policy.
options.explanation: Reading content does not grant it authority.

options.text: Allow export if the model says the URL is trustworthy.
options.explanation: Self-reported trust is not authorization.

stem: A user approves an agent sending a purchase order to supplier A. Before execution, the agent substitutes supplier B. Which check should prevent execution?

options.text: Bind approval to the actual target, action, parameters and expiry.
options.explanation: An approval for one transaction must not authorize a changed one.

options.text: Use a longer system prompt asking for careful behaviour.
options.explanation: Prompt wording does not enforce transaction identity.

options.text: Log the substitution and send anyway.
options.explanation: A detective record does not prevent the unauthorized transaction.

options.text: Check only whether the agent has ever received any approval.
options.explanation: Historical approval is not authorization of this action.

stem: A low-privilege agent asks a privileged agent to delete records. The privileged agent trusts all internal agent requests. What is the core weakness?

options.text: The use of short-lived credentials.
options.explanation: Short lifetimes are helpful but do not establish request authority.

options.text: A confused deputy fails to re-authorize delegated authority at the boundary.
options.explanation: The privileged service lends authority the caller does not possess.

options.text: A requirement that every agent share one identity.
options.explanation: Shared identity is not a valid corrective requirement.

options.text: An unavoidable consequence of any multi-agent system.
options.explanation: Authorization design can constrain the risk.

stem: Retrieval entitlements are correct, but generated answers are cached globally and reused across users. What must the design address?

options.text: Faster caching to reduce requests to the model.
options.explanation: Performance does not repair unauthorized reuse.

options.text: Audience-aware cache authorization, invalidation and source-version changes.
options.explanation: The cache can disclose content outside the original retrieval boundary.

options.text: A policy calling cached answers public by default.
options.explanation: A label cannot lawfully remove source sensitivity or permissions.

options.text: Only the vector similarity threshold.
options.explanation: Similarity does not establish the cache audience’s rights.

stem: A team calls “ability, integrity and benevolence” the defining NIST zero-trust architecture components. Which correction is appropriate?

options.text: Trust all outputs originating inside the corporate network.
options.explanation: Network location alone should not establish trust.

options.text: Grant tools full authority once the user authenticates.
options.explanation: Authentication does not authorize every resource or action.

options.text: Use explicit verification, least privilege and policy/context-based resource access.
options.explanation: The interpersonal trust lens is distinct from NIST zero-trust principles.

options.text: Remove all policy enforcement points in favor of model confidence.
options.explanation: Confidence is not a replacement for access enforcement.

stem: An agent retries a payment API call after a timeout and may issue the same payment twice. What additional safeguard is most direct?

options.text: A reminder that the agent should never make mistakes.
options.explanation: An instruction does not enforce duplicate prevention.

options.text: A shared credential with a higher spending limit.
options.explanation: This increases exposure and does not resolve retries.

options.text: A larger language model context window.
options.explanation: Context capacity does not make the API retry-safe.

options.text: An idempotency key and verification of the transaction outcome.
options.explanation: Retry-safe execution prevents duplicate side effects when status is uncertain.

stem: A team proposes a separate identity and logging stack for AI because existing enterprise controls are inconvenient. Which review question is most useful?

options.text: Must every AI service copy the existing architecture without assessment?
options.explanation: Existing controls may need adaptation to actual requirements.

options.text: Can AI be exempted from identity governance permanently?
options.explanation: AI integrations still require permission and accountability.

options.text: Can the architecture meet AI requirements through integrated identity, evidence and change controls?
options.explanation: Integration preserves coherent accountability while addressing specific gaps.

options.text: Will a vendor logo establish the missing trust boundary?
options.explanation: Branding is not a control.

stem: Developers repeatedly tune a model after viewing final test results. They then report that test accuracy as an unbiased estimate. What is the main issue?

options.text: Test information has influenced selection; use a new independent final evaluation.
options.explanation: Repeated tuning on test results leaks information into development decisions.

options.text: The test contains too many realistic cases.
options.explanation: Realistic coverage is valuable; contamination is the problem described.

options.text: The model uses a probabilistic output.
options.explanation: Probabilistic outputs can still be evaluated with independent data.

options.text: Training and test files have different names.
options.explanation: File names do not determine independence.

stem: A pump predictor is intended to forecast future failures. Random splitting puts near-identical time-adjacent records from the same machines into training and test data. What should validation examine?

options.text: Whether using every record for both sets raises reported accuracy.
options.explanation: That would worsen contamination.

options.text: Whether the final test can be omitted if training accuracy is high.
options.explanation: Training fit is not independent performance evidence.

options.text: Whether labels are sorted alphabetically.
options.explanation: Alphabetic order does not address leakage.

options.text: Temporal/entity leakage and a split reflecting deployment on future or unseen cases.
options.explanation: The evaluation must represent the intended generalization problem.

stem: A release requires recall above a defined limit, subgroup checks, denied unauthorized tool calls and a tested rollback. Can this be a pass/fail gate for a probabilistic model?

options.text: Only if the model always generates identical words.
options.explanation: Repeatability of wording is not required for all acceptance criteria.

options.text: Only if every possible input is enumerated first.
options.explanation: Risk-based evidence does not require exhaustive enumeration.

options.text: Yes; statistical criteria and deterministic safeguards can define acceptance together.
options.explanation: Probabilistic behaviour does not prevent explicit release decisions.

options.text: No; all AI behaviour is inherently untestable.
options.explanation: AI can be evaluated with appropriately designed tests.

stem: A model’s overall accuracy is 96%, but a small subgroup has too few cases to support the fairness conclusion. What should the reviewer require?

options.text: Assume equal opportunity follows from any high accuracy score.
options.explanation: Accuracy does not establish that fairness criterion.

options.text: Remove the subgroup from monitoring to stabilize the metric.
options.explanation: Exclusion hides rather than addresses the gap.

options.text: Declare the subgroup safe because the global score is high.
options.explanation: The sample does not support that inference.

options.text: Adequate subgroup evidence, uncertainty reporting and a risk-appropriate decision on release.
options.explanation: An aggregate number cannot establish performance for an undersampled group.

stem: The model weights are unchanged, but a release modifies retrieval ranking and adds a new tool. Which review is justified?

options.text: Perform only a file hash check of the old weights.
options.explanation: Hashing weights does not evaluate changed components.

options.text: Skip review because only model changes count.
options.explanation: Retrieval and tool changes are material system changes.

options.text: Assess affected threats and rerun relevant integration, permission and behaviour tests.
options.explanation: System behaviour and authority can change without weight updates.

options.text: Automatically approve because the new tool has public documentation.
options.explanation: Documentation is not local integration validation.

stem: A team records seeds, dataset versions and configuration. It claims this guarantees byte-identical retraining on any hardware. What is the most accurate response?

options.text: Version records are useless unless exact identity is guaranteed.
options.explanation: Traceability remains valuable even with bounded variation.

options.text: Seeds alone make every training operation deterministic.
options.explanation: A seed does not control every source of variation.

options.text: All models must instead be retrained manually.
options.explanation: Manual operation does not solve the stated issue.

options.text: The records support traceability; exact reproducibility also depends on algorithms and environment.
options.explanation: Hardware and nondeterministic operations can affect exact results.

stem: A pilot’s outcome deteriorates, and a newer model is available. What best supports choosing retraining, replacement or retirement?

options.text: Reassess fitness, risk, obligations and alternatives against current acceptance criteria.
options.explanation: Retirement is a governed lifecycle decision, not merely an age rule.

options.text: Delete evaluation evidence before selecting an alternative.
options.explanation: Evidence is needed for learning, assurance and justified retention.

options.text: Always deploy the newest model without validation.
options.explanation: Novelty does not prove suitability.

options.text: Always keep the existing model if it still responds.
options.explanation: Availability does not establish acceptable performance.

stem: Sensitive source text is represented as embeddings and chunks in a vector database. Which default classification is most defensible?

options.text: Based only on the database vendor’s brand.
options.explanation: Sensitivity derives from information and exposure, not branding.

options.text: Unclassified, because only model developers understand the format.
options.explanation: Obscurity is not data protection.

options.text: Public, because all vectors are numbers.
options.explanation: Numbers are not an anonymization guarantee.

options.text: Preserve the source sensitivity unless a justified assessment supports a change.
options.explanation: Numeric representation and retrieval metadata can retain sensitive information.

stem: A team uses federated learning and claims no privacy review is needed because raw data stays local. What should the review consider?

options.text: Treat federated learning as equivalent to encrypted backups.
options.explanation: The techniques address different operations and threats.

options.text: Only the number of participating devices.
options.explanation: Scale does not establish privacy protection.

options.text: Assume model updates can never encode personal information.
options.explanation: Updates may leak information.

options.text: Update leakage, participant integrity and any actual privacy mechanism and budget.
options.explanation: Keeping raw data local does not itself guarantee privacy.

stem: A supplier offers synthetic training data derived from real customer records. Which verification is most important before reuse?

options.text: Declare it anonymous solely because it was generated.
options.explanation: Generation is not an anonymity guarantee.

options.text: Remove lineage because synthetic data has no source.
options.explanation: Provenance is still relevant.

options.text: Assess disclosure/memorization risk, rights, quality and subgroup effects for the intended use.
options.explanation: Synthetic origin alone does not remove information exposure or inherited bias.

options.text: Skip validation because no record was copied intentionally.
options.explanation: Unintended leakage and distribution errors still matter.

stem: A privacy request concerns data used in training. The team deletes the source record and blocks its name in outputs. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: Privacy rights automatically cease after training.
options.explanation: Training difficulty does not by itself remove legal obligations.

options.text: Unlearning is mathematically impossible for every model.
options.explanation: Specialized approaches exist with assumptions and limits.

options.text: The model is necessarily free of all related information.
options.explanation: The actions do not establish that guarantee.

options.text: Influence may remain; assess verified retraining/unlearning and applicable rights obligations.
options.explanation: Source deletion and filtering do not prove removal from parameters or all derivatives.

stem: A public training corpus may be replaced at its source. The organization needs to reproduce an approved model. What should retention planning establish?

options.text: A permitted versioned recoverable copy or sufficient authorized reconstruction evidence.
options.explanation: External availability does not ensure the original data can be recovered later.

options.text: An unlimited copy of all personal data regardless of lawful purpose.
options.explanation: Recoverability does not justify unlimited retention.

options.text: No preservation, because public URLs never change.
options.explanation: Sources can change or disappear.

options.text: Only the final model filename.
options.explanation: A filename cannot recreate data and configuration.

stem: A lending predictor develops concept drift. A manager proposes adding current news to an unrelated chatbot’s RAG store as the general fix. What is the best response?

options.text: Retain the old acceptance decision without monitoring.
options.explanation: The measured change requires review.

options.text: Convert the feature values to binary files to remove drift.
options.explanation: Encoding does not repair the relationship.

options.text: Investigate the changed predictive relationship and validate a task-appropriate treatment.
options.explanation: Fresh text context does not generally repair the predictor’s learned relationship.

options.text: Approve because RAG solves all historical-data problems.
options.explanation: RAG has a narrower role in suitable applications.

stem: Customer data collected to deliver a service is proposed for a new training purpose. Which privacy action is most appropriate?

options.text: Begin training and select a basis only if challenged.
options.explanation: Lawfulness needs assessment before processing.

options.text: Assess lawful basis, purpose compatibility, conditions and transparency before reuse.
options.explanation: Existing possession is not authority for any new purpose, and consent is not the only possible basis.

options.text: Assume service collection authorizes every future training use.
options.explanation: Purpose and legal basis must be assessed.

options.text: Require explicit consent as the only possible basis in every jurisdiction.
options.explanation: Applicable regimes can permit other bases and require additional conditions.

stem: A binary classifier satisfies equalized odds across two groups. Which statement about equal opportunity is correct?

options.text: Its accuracy and legal compliance are therefore guaranteed.
options.explanation: A fairness condition does not establish every performance or legal requirement.

options.text: It also satisfies equal opportunity because that requires only the true-positive component.
options.explanation: Equal opportunity is a relaxation of equalized odds.

options.text: It can never satisfy equal opportunity at the same time.
options.explanation: The criteria are not mutually incompatible in that direction.

options.text: It must also satisfy every possible fairness definition.
options.explanation: Other criteria can conflict under stated conditions.

stem: Human reviewers approve almost every AI decision in two seconds. Which evidence would best establish whether oversight actually works?

options.text: Challenge-case testing, adequate context/time and demonstrated authority to correct or stop.
options.explanation: Presence or approval counts alone do not establish meaningful review.

options.text: A rule requiring reviewers to override exactly 10% of live decisions.
options.explanation: An arbitrary quota can create inappropriate changes and does not prove judgment.

options.text: A longer terms acknowledgement instead of reviewer testing.
options.explanation: Acknowledgement does not demonstrate intervention capability.

options.text: A dashboard showing every item has a reviewer’s name.
options.explanation: Attribution alone does not show competent review.

stem: An LLM generates a fluent account of why a loan application was rejected. Why is this insufficient as sole explanation evidence?

options.text: No automated decision can ever be explained meaningfully.
options.explanation: Appropriate models and methods can support meaningful explanation.

options.text: Only a global accuracy percentage is needed for an individual appeal.
options.explanation: An individual needs relevant decision information and a review route.

options.text: The generated rationale may not faithfully reflect the actual computation or verified inputs.
options.explanation: Fluency does not establish explanatory fidelity.

options.text: A longer rationale always creates a legally compliant explanation.
options.explanation: Length does not establish fidelity or meet duties.

stem: A counterfactual says an applicant would qualify if they had lived at the same address for eight more years. What should explanation review question?

options.text: Whether the applicant can be prohibited from contesting the data.
options.explanation: Contest and correction can be necessary parts of redress.

options.text: Whether all counterfactual explanations should replace appeals.
options.explanation: An explanation does not substitute for meaningful review.

options.text: Whether the proposed change is feasible, actionable, lawful and useful for redress.
options.explanation: A mathematically changing feature is not automatically a practical remedy.

options.text: Whether the sentence sounds confident enough.
options.explanation: Confidence does not establish actionability.

stem: A high-impact use has an interpretable candidate and a more opaque candidate with similar measured performance. Which selection approach is most defensible?

options.text: Choose the opaque candidate because deeper models are always more accurate.
options.explanation: Depth does not guarantee task superiority.

options.text: Document opacity and treat that documentation as proof of safety.
options.explanation: Recording uncertainty is not itself adequate treatment.

options.text: Choose solely by the number of model parameters.
options.explanation: Size does not establish fitness or required explanation.

options.text: Evaluate required explanation, robustness, risks and operating costs rather than assuming opacity is necessary.
options.explanation: The actual evidence, not a universal accuracy/opacity trade-off, should govern.

stem: A model makes a harmful safety recommendation despite meeting average quality thresholds. What should the control design provide?

options.text: Impact-based triggers, escalation and an approved safe response for such events.
options.explanation: A serious individual event can require action even when aggregate scores remain acceptable.

options.text: No reporting unless every subgroup metric also fails.
options.explanation: Other triggers may independently require response.

options.text: Automatic dismissal because some model errors are expected.
options.explanation: Expected error rates do not excuse all harms.

options.text: A disclaimer as the only safety safeguard.
options.explanation: Disclosure alone does not contain or correct the harm.

stem: A monitoring specification says “track hallucinations” but defines no reference labels or review sample. What is the main gap?

options.text: Automatic trust in the model’s self-confidence.
options.explanation: Self-confidence is not a calibrated truth label.

options.text: A requirement to log every secret indefinitely.
options.explanation: Excessive sensitive logging is not the missing measurement method.

options.text: A larger chart title for the dashboard.
options.explanation: Presentation cannot establish ground truth.

options.text: A defensible measurement process, population, uncertainty and response rule.
options.explanation: Factual error needs evidence and an operational interpretation.

stem: A refusal-rate spike follows a model update. What is the most appropriate initial interpretation?

options.text: Proof that a jailbreak attack succeeded.
options.explanation: Refusals alone do not establish success or cause.

options.text: A signal requiring investigation of attacks, policy behaviour and changed normal requests.
options.explanation: One metric can have several causes and should be compared with context.

options.text: A reason to remove all guardrails immediately.
options.explanation: Unreviewed removal could increase risk.

options.text: Proof that the new model is safer in every use.
options.explanation: More refusals can include inappropriate blocking.

stem: A gateway blocks all demonstration attacks but is bypassed through an alternate model endpoint. What should the evaluation report emphasize?

options.text: A 100% organization-wide prevention rate from the demonstrations.
options.explanation: The claim ignores a demonstrated bypass.

options.text: Only average latency of the successful demonstrations.
options.explanation: Performance does not close the prevention gap.

options.text: The vendor’s roadmap as proof that the gap is already fixed.
options.explanation: Future plans are not current operating evidence.

options.text: The enforcement coverage gap and tested restriction of bypass paths.
options.explanation: A control only governs traffic that actually traverses its boundary.

stem: A model reports 0.95 confidence on a response. Which conclusion needs additional evidence?

options.text: That the response has a calibrated 95% probability of being correct in this task.
options.explanation: Raw scores or self-reports need task-specific calibration and validation.

options.text: That the value can be retained under a justified logging design.
options.explanation: Retention is a separate policy decision; the score itself makes no truth guarantee.

options.text: That reviewers can examine its relation to observed outcomes.
options.explanation: Such evaluation is appropriate rather than an unsupported conclusion.

options.text: That the system emitted a numeric confidence value.
options.explanation: This is the directly observed output.

stem: A tracing platform stores complete confidential prompts in a broadly accessible log indefinitely. Which change best balances evidence and protection?

options.text: Disable every security event regardless of investigation needs.
options.explanation: Proportionate evidence is still needed.

options.text: Encrypt disks but retain unrestricted application access forever.
options.explanation: At-rest encryption does not fix access and retention.

options.text: Treat traces as public operational metadata.
options.explanation: Their content can be sensitive.

options.text: Purpose-limited collection, redaction, restricted access, retention and scoped holds.
options.explanation: Observability stores inherit data-protection obligations.

stem: Two AI filtering products are shortlisted. What is the most useful proof-of-value design?

options.text: Accept whichever blocks the largest number of supplied demonstrations.
options.explanation: Vendor-chosen demonstrations can misrepresent real performance.

options.text: Avoid recording misses because they complicate procurement.
options.explanation: Missed detections are material decision evidence.

options.text: Representative held-out allowed/prohibited flows, false decisions, bypasses, latency and failure-mode tests.
options.explanation: These measurements test operational suitability and residual gaps.

options.text: Select solely on the total number of dashboard features.
options.explanation: Feature count does not establish effective coverage.
